text:
The construction is coherent as an episode, but it contains at least one specific defect that I think is established by the frozen material rather than merely proposed. The defect is not in P7, P9, or the E009 criticism. It is in the construct's central claim that P9's correlation objection "splits" the snapshot-as-a-whole target into a bound-arithmetic target and a bound-correspondence target. That split is not a distinction the source's target taxonomy can carry without a change the construct does not acknowledge, and the construct's own framing of the split quietly imports a standpoint — realizability under an unstated resource model — that P7 lists separately from the snapshot-as-a-whole target.

The relevant P7 text is:

> "One can criticize a reconstruction rule, a particular record, a booking's history, the snapshot as a whole, or the assumption that logical time is meaningful."

The list has five items, and the last three are different *types* of thing: a booking's history is a temporal sequence of records, the snapshot as a whole is the current aggregate, and "the assumption that logical time is meaningful" is neither a record nor an aggregate but a background presupposition. P9's correlation objection concerns "a physical resource not named in the snapshot." That unnamed resource is not a record, not a booking's history, not the snapshot as a whole, and not the meaningfulness of logical time. It is a presupposition about the modeled world — specifically, that capacity is the only relevant shared constraint. The construct's "bound-correspondence target" is therefore best understood, in P7's own taxonomy, as a criticism of a *source assumption* (compare P7's later remark: "one can reject a rule while accepting the data, or accept the rule while rejecting the data as corrupt or late"), not as a subdivision of the snapshot-as-a-whole target.

The construct does not say this. Instead it asserts:

> "I propose that the correlation objection actually splits P7's 'snapshot-as-a-whole' target into two further targets…"

That is a claim about P7's taxonomy that P7's taxonomy does not support. P7's list is exhaustive in the local sense that it names the kinds of things a criticism can address; adding a "bound-correspondence target" inside "snapshot-as-a-whole" attributes to the snapshot an external-comparison component that P7 assigns, if anywhere, to source assumptions. The construct's own Objection 3 half-acknowledges this:

> "If someone thinks P7's list of targets is exhaustive and indivisible, the split is a disagreement with P7's taxonomy, not with P9's objection."

But the construct then declines to resolve the flag, and elsewhere it proceeds as if the split were a reading of P7 rather than a revision of it. That is the specific defect: an unsupported re-classification of a source target, presented as a subdivision rather than as a proposed amendment.

The distinction matters because the two readings of the correlation objection give different answers to the construct's guiding question. Under the re-classification reading, P9's objection does not force any change to a P7-respecting account of global availability *as an account of the snapshot*; it forces a change to an account of what the snapshot is being used to describe, which P7's target list already marks as a distinct target ("the assumption that logical time is meaningful" — and, by extension, other source assumptions). Under the subdivision reading, the objection falls inside the availability account itself, and some change to that account is required. The construct switches between these readings. It says, correctly under the re-classification reading:

> "No change is required to the availability arithmetic if 'availability' is read as the interval over the product of per-booking possibility sets."

And it also says, under the subdivision reading:

> "A change is required to any claim that this interval characterizes what the warehouse can actually do."

Both sentences can be true, but they answer different questions, and the construct treats them as one account rather than two. The P7-respecting way to keep both is to say that the correlation objection targets a *source assumption about what the snapshot models*, not the availability account's internal consistency. P7 already provides the slot; the construct does not use it.

A second, smaller defect compounds the first. The E009 criticism, on the construct's reading, "does not engage P9's correspondence-side objection, because WHL has no primitive for joint realizability beyond the capacity sum." That is accurate as far as it goes, but the construct then says:

> "The E009 criticism actually notes this… That proposed repair names the correspondence side, but E009 treats it as one item in a list rather than as the item that survives every repair of the arithmetic side. My construction moves it to the front and says which half of P9 it belongs to."

"Which half of P9 it belongs to" is exactly the question the construct has not settled, because it has not decided whether the correspondence side is a target inside the availability account or a source assumption outside it. So the construct claims to have moved the E009 item to the front and assigned it, when in fact it has moved it to the front and left its assignment to P7's taxonomy open. That is not an error in the E009 criticism; it is an unfinished move in the construction.

I want to be careful about what I am and am not claiming. I am not claiming that the construct's split is false, or that a revised target taxonomy would be unwarranted. The construct's own Objection 4 ("Doesn't the correspondence failure only matter if you care about physical realizability? Yes.") is a candid acknowledgment that the split's relevance depends on a stipulated question. What I am claiming is narrower and I think established by the sources: the split is not a reading of P7's target list, because P7 already supplies a target for external presuppositions about what the snapshot models, and the construct does not notice this. Presenting the split as a subdivision of "snapshot-as-a-whole" loses the distinction P7 was careful to draw between criticizing the object and criticizing the assumption under which the object is read. That is a lost distinction, not a mere stylistic choice.

A rival reading is available that keeps the construct intact: perhaps by "snapshot as a whole" P7 meant something broad enough to include the snapshot's implicit modeling commitments, so that the split is genuinely internal to that target. If so, the construct's proposal is compatible with P7 and my criticism fails. The construct does not supply textual support for this broader reading, and P7's separate mention of "the assumption that logical time is meaningful" weighs against it. I note this as an open interpretive question rather than as a settled defect, but I do think the burden falls on the broader reading, since P7's list is otherwise composed of items at clearly different levels of abstraction, and the level occupied by "the assumption that…" is the natural home for "the assumption that capacity is the only shared constraint."

One further point, since the carrier is unconstrained prose and I should not over-formalize: the construct's insistence that "this is not a new language component" is defensible if and only if the split is read as a re-description of what "availability" names. But whether an account of global availability implicitly claims correspondence is not something the account can settle by re-description alone; it depends on what downstream consumers of the account are entitled to infer. P9's criticism — "exposing alternatives without a policy for resolving them pushes the problem downstream, where it may be resolved badly or inconsistently" — is precisely about this entitlement, and the construct's split does not touch it. So even on the construct's own reading, the correlation objection and the downstream-resolution objection pull in different directions: the first can be absorbed by re-description, the second cannot. The construct presents them as if they belonged to the same layer. That, too, is a small but specific loss of distinction, and it is one the frozen packet already contains in P9.

Bottom line: the construction adds a useful distinction and connects P7 and P9 in a way neither contains alone. But its central move — treating the bound-correspondence target as an internal subdivision of P7's snapshot-as-a-whole target — is not supported by P7's own target list, which already contains a distinct slot for assumptions about what the snapshot models. Either the construct should present the split as a proposed amendment to P7's taxonomy, or it should re-locate the correspondence side to the source-assumption target. As written, it does neither, and that is a defect established by the frozen material rather than merely conjectured.
